answer: To sit on a ballot, an agent must reserve a bonded slice of a real power feeder at a substation on a windward ridge, and publish five-minute meter receipts signed by the utility. Mid-window a randomly chosen raven auditor requests a live current-voltage trace; that trace is passed through a prism of harmonic bins and must match the feeder's enrolled signature. Keys that share one meter, or spoof from a bench battery, fail the harmonics and forfeit the bond. A sybil inventory then costs as many distinct feeders as it wants votes.
